newsitem.title: TAIWAN: FORECAST-Taiwan May export orders seen up 5.08 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Taiwan May export orders seen up 5.08 pct.

text.p: A Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists on Thursday projected modest year-on-year growth of 5.082 percent for Taiwan's export orders in May, with the rise due chiefly to firm demand from Europe and the United States.
The figures were due to be released by the economics ministry at 0230 GMT on June 21.
In April, export orders rose 5.91 percent year-on-year.
The following table lists institutions' forecasts for year-on-year change in May export orders in percent:
Institution change (yr/yr)
Core Pacific Securities 5.0
Grand Cathay Securities 3.0
HSBC James Capel Taiwan 4.76
National Securities 5.0
Nomura Securities 7.65
Average 5.082
Economists said they expected higher export order growth from Europe and the United States.

"We may receive more orders, especially for information and telecommunications products, from Europe and the United States, whose economies have shown sound recovery," said Nomura Securities economist Amy Huang.
The Taiwan dollar's gradual depreciation against the U.S. dollar and the Japanese yen in recent weeks also should boost Taiwan exporters' competitiveness worldwide.
"The recent Taiwan dollar depreciation should help boost our export orders and then exports growth," said National Securities economist Lin Kuo-yang.
The Taiwan dollar long hovered around T$27.5 to the U.S. dollar, but has slipped slowly in 1997 to around T$27.9.
Economists said they expected the local dollar's fall to show an effect on exports in the third quarter.

"The Taiwan dollar depreciation will trigger higher growth in exports from the star electronics, information technology and telecommunications sectors in the third quarter," said Core Pacific Securities economist Lin Yang-chuan.

Economists said the orders growth would still be offset in part by the loss of US$130 million a month in foreign orders for pork since late March following an islandwide outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease on Taiwan's hog farms.
-- James Peng, Taipei newsroom (886-2-5080815)
